title: The Effect of Problem-Based Learning Integrated with Artificial Intelligence on Self-Regulated Learning Tendencies
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether Problem-Based Learning (PBL) integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) can strengthen junior high school students’ self-regulated learning (SRL) tendencies. The authors frame the study around a gap in prior research: although PBL and AI-supported learning have each been linked to SRL, fewer studies have tested AI as an adaptive scaffolding component within PBL, especially in school settings.

The intervention was implemented as an AI-integrated PBL lesson design that supported students through problem orientation, investigation, solution development, presentation, and reflection. AI was described as providing guided support such as prompts, feedback, scaffolding, and information exploration assistance rather than being used simply as a standalone technology. The study used a one-group posttest-only quasi-experimental design, with SRL measured by a Likert-scale questionnaire covering goal setting, strategy use, self-monitoring, time and resource management, motivational control, and self-reflection.

The participants were 60 seventh-grade students from SMP Negeri 1 Telaga Biru in Indonesia, drawn purposively from two classes during the first semester of the 2025/2026 academic year. Quantitative analysis used normality testing followed by either a one-sample t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test against a reference value. The results showed SRL scores in the good-to-high range and significantly above the benchmark in both classes. The strongest areas were forethought, motivational belief, and self-reflection, while help-seeking and collaboration were comparatively weaker. The authors conclude that AI-integrated PBL can positively support SRL, but social regulation components such as peer collaboration and structured help-seeking still need to be deliberately designed.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental study, but it uses a one-group posttest-only design with no comparison group or pretest, which limits internal validity and causal inference. The paper also reports no effect sizes for the main outcomes, further reducing evidentiary strength.
impact_tier_rationale: The study suggests a positive effect on SRL tendencies, but the practical magnitude is unclear because effect sizes are not reported and the design is criterion-referenced rather than comparative. The findings are promising for a priority population (junior high students) but remain modest and uncertain in generalizability.

interventions.use_case: problem-based learning integrated with AI-based pedagogical scaffolding, including prompts, guided information exploration, rapid feedback, and reflection support for grade 7 junior high students

finding.finding_summary: In a quasi-experimental one-group posttest-only study of 60 grade 7 students (n=30 in VII-1; n=30 in VII-3), AI-integrated PBL was associated with good-to-high self-regulated learning tendencies. SRL scores were significantly above the reference value of 75 in both classes: VII-1 showed a one-sample t-test result of t=15.777, p<.001, mean difference=11.56, 95% CI [10.06, 13.06], while VII-3 showed a Wilcoxon signed-rank result of Z=4.792, p<.001.
finding.measure: Self-regulated learning questionnaire/survey covering goal setting, strategy use, self-monitoring, time/resource management, motivational control, and self-reflection

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports a strong post-intervention SRL profile, especially in forethought, performance/control, and self-reflection, which are durable-skill components of metacognition and self-management. However, help-seeking and collaboration were comparatively lower, suggesting the intervention strengthened individual regulation more than social regulation.
finding.measure: SRL indicator scores by dimension (forethought, performance/implementation & control, motivational belief, self-control & persistence, help-seeking & collaboration, self-reflection/evaluation)
